title: The ShellObject contract
summary: Every shell object inherits the ShellObject mixin: ordered fields and field(name), table/json for ~~table~~json chaining, asTable/asJson, identity and isCurrent (a kept object must not silently become a different resource: LinuxProcess identity is pid plus start time), generation/refresh, source, capabilities (READ by default), keep(name) onto the ScratchPad, and describe(name), which tells an LLM the class, fields, public and protected methods and SHELL_HELP note, built from the class so it cannot drift. ShellCollection shows lists (sortedBy, first, select; mixed rows allowed).
authority: built and tested (architecture Tom Dyer; coding and writing Claude (Opus 5.5), 2026-11-24)
invariants: describe() is generated from the class, never written by hand

No shell class takes the name of an ooRexx built-in class; filesystem classes carry the Fs prefix (FsFile, FsFolder): .File is ooRexx's and .Directory is a collection, not C:\Windows or /etc (Tom Dyer, 2026-11-24)
A class gives the LLM its semantics in a SHELL_HELP constant
Long values in tables keep their tail (paths end in what matters)
procedure: New objects: inherit ShellObject, define fields, add SHELL_HELP, mark anything that changes state PROTECTED, give authorityPath (and authorityAction if the method name is too coarse)

provenance.claim: ShellObject, ShellCollection, ScratchPad, describe, shellPublicMethods, shellProtectedMethods
